The video was him aimlessly poking around while the installer ran, but he answered two important questions I had.

Linux Mint is based on the LTS releases of Ubuntu. That's great for me because those are the Ubuntu releases I run.

You can use regular Ubuntu PPAs in Mint. Aside from giving you software not available in the main repositories, PPAs let you run the latest version of software if you need some features that are not in the repo's version. Not having the newest software features is the main problem with LTS releases, but it's usually only a few things you use a lot. PPAs are the nicest fix for that. You're not stuck with what's in the repo.
